title: Stringmaster
statementMd:
After years of training, you have finally awakened your true power and become a stringmaster, allowing you to perform the following operation on a string:

Choose a subsequence∗∗ that is a palindrome†† and arbitrarily permute the characters at the selected positions.

Here is an example of such an operation where we select the palindrome `tst`: testing→setting

𝚝𝚎𝚜𝚝𝚒𝚗𝚐→𝚜𝚎𝚝𝚝𝚒𝚗𝚐

Now you have a string x𝑥, and you want to know if you can turn it into a string y by performing the above operation any number of times (possibly zero).

∗A string a is a subsequence of a string b if a can be obtained from b by the deletion of several (possibly zero or all) characters.

†A string is called a palindrome if it is the same when written in reverse order. For example, `eertree` and `abba` are palindromes.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1≤t≤104). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains a single integer n (1≤n≤2⋅105) — the length of the strings x and y.

The second line of each test case contains a string x of length n consisting of lowercase Latin letters.

The third line of each test case contains a string y of length n consisting of lowercase Latin letters.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅105.

## Output

For each test case, output `YES` if you can turn x into y, and `NO` otherwise.

You can output `YES` and `NO` in any case (for example, `yES`, `yes`, and `Yes` will be accepted).

## Note

The solution to the first test case is shown above.

In the second test case, it is not possible to change the string.

In the third test case, no operations are needed.
